newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ASTRA SAYS WORKING ON LOSEC REPLACEMENT.
newsitem.headline: ASTRA SAYS WORKING ON LOSEC REPLACEMENT.

text.p: Swedish drugs group Astra said on Thursday that an agent that recently entered phase III of clinical trials in Europe and the U.S. was intended to replace its top selling drug, anti-ulcer agent Losec.
"Just as Losec, it (the drug) is a long acting acid-pump inhibitor but with a different medical profile," Astra spokesman Staffan Ternby told Reuters.
"You can compare it with (beta-blocker) Seloken and Seloken ZOC where Seloken ZOC largely has replaced Seloken," he said.
It is, however, hard to know how the Losec replacement will stand up to competition when Losec patents start expiring in 2001, Ternby said.
"Medically, it can replace Losec but then it is another assessment how it can stand up commercially against generic Losec copies," he said.
Ternby refrained from disclosing when the new drug could be registered.
Losec is Astra's biggest selling product, with its own sales accounting for 10.02 billion crowns of sales of 21.47 billion crowns in the first half of 1997.
But analysts have voiced concern about the company being left with a huge gap when patents for Astra start expiring.
Ternby added Astra was working on a replacement for its anti-asthma treatment Turbuhaler.
"We have (previously) chosen to improve the Turbuhaler instead of launching new inhalers but now we have a follower to the Turbuhaler in our laboratories," Ternby said.
"It is still a powder inhaler and Astra is most likely to continue with the Turbuhaler concept. But we have made larger changes to the followers than we so far have done to the Turbuhaler."
The new inhalers are mainly aimed at asthma treatment.
